div.head: [Untitled]
div.p: William Anderson, Saxon & Co., shipped in good order and condition, by, in, and upon the good ship called the Earl of Marr and Kellie, Captain J. Still, now riding at anchor in Table bay and bound for Angra Pequena, two hundred and fifty tons coal, (to be taken from alongside the ship within ten days, at the expense and risk of the consignee, the captain rendering all assistance in his power in landing the coals,) being marked and numbered as in the margin, and are to be delivered in the like good order and condition, at the aforesaid port of Angra Pequena, (the act of God, the Queen’s enemies, fire, and all and every other dangers and accidents of the seas, rivers, and navigation of whatever nature and kind soever, excepted,) unto order, or to my assigns. Freight for the said goods being paid here, say 20 shillings per ton, without primage and average accustomed. In witness whereof, the master or purser of the said ship hath affirmed to four bills of lading, all of this tenor and date, one of which bills being accomplished, the other three to stand void.
Received a quantity of coals, weight unknown.
